title: A DNS TXT record can contain multiple count strings
summary: The RDATA of TXT can be composed of multiple character-strings, and the first byte of each segment gives the length of this segment.
detail: Two paragraphs of text in one record are not equal to two independent responses; the original data can be restored by skipping the length bytes one by one.
boundary: How to splice segments between segments is agreed upon by the upper layer at the application layer, and the protocol does not automatically insert spaces or newlines.
relevance: When restoring text from offline DNS records, avoid mixing length bytes or display spaces into the content.
